en: My phone battery drains very fast these days.
tamil: இப்பல்லாம் என் போன் பேட்டரி ரொம்ப சீக்கிரம் தீர்ந்துடுது.
context: Complaining about a weak phone battery.
explain: Present simple shows a regular habit or problem. 'These days' means recently.
usage: Say it to a friend or at a mobile shop when your phone needs repair.
leelaQ: How is your phone battery these days?
answer: My phone battery is good, but it needs charging twice a day.

en: I forgot my Wi-Fi password again.
tamil: நான் மறுபடியும் என் வைஃபை பாஸ்வேர்டை மறந்துட்டேன்.
context: Telling a family member you forgot the Wi-Fi password.
explain: 'Forgot' is the past of 'forget'. 'Again' shows it has happened before.
usage: Use it at home when you cannot connect a device to the internet.
leelaQ: Do you remember all your passwords?
answer: No, I forget them often, so I write them in a notebook.

en: The video call is not clear because the internet is slow.
tamil: இன்டர்நெட் ஸ்லோவா இருக்கறதால வீடியோ கால் தெளிவா இல்ல.
context: Explaining a bad video call to a colleague.
explain: 'Because' gives the reason. 'Is not' makes the sentence negative.
usage: Say it in an online meeting when others cannot hear or see you well.
leelaQ: What do you do when the internet is slow?
answer: I restart the router and wait for a few minutes.

en: I will send you the file on WhatsApp in five minutes.
tamil: நான் அஞ்சு நிமிஷத்துல உனக்கு ஃபைலை வாட்ஸ்அப்ல அனுப்புறேன்.
context: Promising to share a file with a friend.
explain: 'Will' shows a promise about the future. 'In five minutes' tells when.
usage: Use it with friends or coworkers who are waiting for a document.
leelaQ: How do you share photos with your family?
answer: I send them on WhatsApp because everyone uses it.

en: Please turn off your mic when you are not speaking.
tamil: நீங்க பேசாதப்போ தயவுசெஞ்சு உங்க மைக்கை ஆஃப் பண்ணுங்க.
context: Asking participants in an online meeting to mute.
explain: 'Please' makes an order polite. 'When' joins two ideas about time.
usage: A meeting host can say this when there is background noise.
leelaQ: Have you ever attended an online meeting?
answer: Yes, I attended one last week with my team.

en: My laptop is hanging, so I cannot finish my work.
tamil: என் லேப்டாப் ஹேங் ஆகுது, அதனால என் வேலையை முடிக்க முடியல.
context: Telling your manager about a computer problem.
explain: 'So' shows the result. 'Cannot' means you are not able to do something.
usage: Use it at the office when a computer problem delays your work.
leelaQ: What do you do when your laptop hangs?
answer: I close extra apps and restart it.

en: Could you share your screen so that we can see the slides?
tamil: நாங்க ஸ்லைடுகளைப் பார்க்க உங்க ஸ்கிரீனை ஷேர் பண்ண முடியுமா?
context: Asking a presenter in an online meeting.
explain: 'Could you' is a polite request. 'So that' gives the purpose.
usage: Use it in a video meeting when someone is explaining something.
leelaQ: How do you present your ideas in a meeting?
answer: I make simple slides and explain them slowly.

en: I have already updated the app, but it still crashes.
tamil: நான் ஆப்பை ஏற்கனவே அப்டேட் பண்ணிட்டேன், ஆனாலும் அது க்ராஷ் ஆகுது.
context: Reporting an app problem to customer support.
explain: 'Have updated' shows an action that is finished but matters now. 'Still' shows the problem continues.
usage: Say it to customer support when an app does not work properly.
leelaQ: Which app do you use the most?
answer: I use WhatsApp the most, for chatting and calling.

en: Never share your OTP with anyone.
tamil: உன் ஓடிபியை யார்கிட்டயும் ஷேர் பண்ணாதே.
context: Warning a family member about online fraud.
explain: 'Never' makes a strong negative order. An OTP is a secret code for safe payments.
usage: Say it to parents or friends to keep them safe from online cheating.
leelaQ: How can we stay safe from online fraud?
answer: We should never share our OTP or bank details with anyone.

en: She is posting photos of her trip on Instagram.
tamil: அவ தன்னோட டிரிப் போட்டோக்களை இன்ஸ்டாகிராம்ல போஸ்ட் பண்ணிட்டு இருக்கா.
context: Telling a friend what someone is doing right now.
explain: Present continuous shows an action happening now. Use 'is' with he, she and it.
usage: Use it when you see a friend's or relative's activity on social media.
leelaQ: Do you post photos on social media?
answer: Yes, I post a few photos when I go to new places.

en: My phone fell down and the screen is cracked.
tamil: என் போன் கீழ விழுந்து ஸ்கிரீன் உடைஞ்சிடுச்சு.
context: Telling a shop owner about a broken phone.
explain: 'Fell' is the past of 'fall'. 'Is cracked' describes the present condition.
usage: Say it at a mobile repair shop to explain the damage.
leelaQ: Has your phone ever fallen and broken?
answer: Yes, it fell from the table once and the screen cracked.

en: Where can I charge my phone?
tamil: என் போனை எங்க சார்ஜ் பண்ணலாம்?
context: Asking for a charging point at a railway station.
explain: 'Where can I...?' asks about a place where something is possible.
usage: Ask at a station, cafe or office when your battery is low.
leelaQ: Where do you usually charge your phone?
answer: I charge it near my bed every night.

en: Can you hear me properly?
tamil: நான் பேசுறது உனக்கு நல்லா கேக்குதா?
context: Checking audio at the start of a call.
explain: 'Can you hear me?' is the standard check at the start of a call. 'Properly' means well.
usage: Use it at the start of a phone or video call.
leelaQ: What do you check before a video call starts?
answer: I check my camera, my mic and my internet.

en: I am going to install a new keyboard app.
tamil: நான் ஒரு புது கீபோர்டு ஆப்பை இன்ஸ்டால் பண்ணப் போறேன்.
context: Telling a friend about a phone plan.
explain: 'Going to' talks about a plan you already made.
usage: Say it when you want to try a new app on your phone.
leelaQ: What new app are you going to try?
answer: I am going to try a language learning app.

en: The meeting link is not working for me.
tamil: மீட்டிங் லிங்க் எனக்கு வேலை செய்யல.
context: Telling the organiser the link does not open.
explain: 'Not working' is a common way to say something does not function.
usage: Message the organiser when you cannot join an online meeting.
leelaQ: What do you do if you cannot join a meeting?
answer: I ask the organiser to send the link again.

en: Please send me the link again.
tamil: தயவுசெஞ்சு லிங்கை மறுபடியும் அனுப்புங்க.
context: Asking a colleague to resend a link.
explain: 'Again' means one more time. 'Please' keeps the request polite.
usage: Use it in chat when a link is lost or has expired.
leelaQ: Who sends you links most often?
answer: My brother sends me funny videos and links.

en: How do I change my profile picture?
tamil: என் ப்ரொஃபைல் படத்தை எப்படி மாத்துறது?
context: Asking a friend for help with an account.
explain: 'How do I...?' asks for steps to do something.
usage: Ask a friend or a helper when you use a new app.
leelaQ: What picture do you keep as your profile photo?
answer: I keep a simple photo of myself smiling.

en: I need to reset my password.
tamil: நான் என் பாஸ்வேர்டை ரீசெட் பண்ணணும்.
context: Telling IT support you are locked out.
explain: 'Need to' shows something necessary. 'Reset' means set again.
usage: Say it to the IT team or customer care when you cannot log in.
leelaQ: When did you last change a password?
answer: I changed my email password last month.

en: I have been using this laptop for five years.
tamil: நான் இந்த லேப்டாப்பை அஞ்சு வருஷமா யூஸ் பண்றேன்.
context: Telling a shop owner how old your laptop is.
explain: 'Have been using' with 'for' shows an action that started in the past and continues.
usage: Say it when you ask if an old device is worth repairing.
leelaQ: How long have you had your phone?
answer: I have had it for two years.

en: Let me check my internet connection.
tamil: நான் என் இன்டர்நெட் கனெக்ஷனை செக் பண்ணிப் பாக்குறேன்.
context: Saying this during a bad call.
explain: 'Let me' is a friendly way to offer to do something.
usage: Use it when a call is breaking and you want a moment to fix it.
leelaQ: What do you do when your call keeps cutting?
answer: I move near the window and call again.

en: Do you have a charger I can borrow?
tamil: நான் வாங்கிக்கிற மாதிரி உன்கிட்ட சார்ஜர் இருக்கா?
context: Asking a colleague for a phone charger.
explain: 'Do you have...?' asks if someone has something. 'I can borrow' tells why you ask.
usage: Ask at the office or in a bus station when your phone is dying.
leelaQ: Do you carry a power bank when you travel?
answer: Yes, I always carry a power bank in my bag.

en: He will join the call after lunch.
tamil: அவன் மதிய சாப்பாட்டுக்கு அப்புறம் கால்ல சேருவான்.
context: Telling the team about someone's availability.
explain: 'Will join' is a simple prediction or plan about the future.
usage: Say it when someone is absent from a meeting but will come later.
leelaQ: When will you join the next meeting?
answer: I will join it at ten o'clock tomorrow.

en: Sorry, I was on mute.
tamil: மன்னிக்கணும், நான் மியூட்ல இருந்தேன்.
context: Apologising in an online meeting.
explain: 'Was' is used with I, he, she and it. 'On mute' means the sound is off.
usage: A very common sentence in online meetings when nobody could hear you.
leelaQ: What happens when someone forgets to unmute?
answer: Everybody waits and says we cannot hear you.

en: My phone is out of storage.
tamil: என் போன்ல ஸ்டோரேஜ் முடிஞ்சிடுச்சு.
context: Complaining that you cannot save more photos.
explain: 'Out of' means there is none left.
usage: Say it when the phone gives a storage full message.
leelaQ: What takes the most space on your phone?
answer: Videos take the most space on my phone.

en: I deleted some old photos to free up space.
tamil: இடம் காலி பண்ண சில பழைய போட்டோக்களை டெலீட் பண்ணினேன்.
context: Explaining how you fixed the storage problem.
explain: 'To free up space' tells the purpose. 'To' plus a verb gives a reason.
usage: Use it when talking about cleaning your phone.
leelaQ: How do you keep your phone clean and fast?
answer: I delete old photos and unused apps every month.
